sections.title: Clinical Oral Surgery I
sections.description: This course is designed to give the student exposure to all aspects of the wide and varied scope of oral and maxillofacial surgery. The course also promotes the integration of the basic sciences and medicine into the daily practice of oral and maxillofacial surgery and dentistry. It builds upon and incorporates knowledge from many prerequisite courses, particularly the Pharmacology, Microbiology, and Anesthesia, Pain, and Anxiety courses. After successful completion of this course and its clinical counterparts (courses #772/773/872/873), the student should be competent in the management of all aspects of oral and maxillofacial surgery as outlined above under the course goals. Lectures will be presented by faculty members of the department of Oral and Maxillofacial surgery. The lecture material and reading assignments are designed to be complementary. The examination will encompass material from both sources. The examination will include questions that reinforce the knowledge obtained by completion of the prerequisite courses of Pharmacology, Microbiology, and OMC V (Anesthesia, Pain, and Anxiety). Students should review the material from those courses as the final examination will contain questions from knowledge obtained by their completion.
